subject: Proposal: Exit gates, acceptance tests and handoff schedule for Oxbridge evaluation
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@oxbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Dan Miller <dan.miller@oxbridgehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP + proposed acceptance tests for PoC

Hi Priya / Dan,

Thanks again for the time earlier this week. Per our call, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that lays out the evaluation objectives, proposed exit gates, and a lightweight test harness we can run against your sample dataset. The attachment is MAP_Oxbridge_v1.xlsx — it contains a week-by-week cadence, owners, and a short list of acceptance tests.

I want to highlight the three candidate exit gates we propose for your eval:
- Performance gate: p50 latency <= 120ms and p95 <= 400ms under representative traffic (1–2 rps steady).
- Quality gate: mean F1 >= 0.92 on the 500-case medical-annotation sample (as agreed in the rubric).
- Operational gate: no more than 2 critical errors (timeouts / model crashes) during a 72h continuous run.

Can you confirm the dataset we should use for the 500-case sample (anonymized), and whether the SLA targets above match what Oxbridge needs for a pilot? If this looks reasonable I’ll convert the acceptance-tests sheet into a runnable checklist and map owners to your SME/engineering contacts.

Proposed timeline (high level):
- Week 0: MAP sign-off and access to test dataset and a test account.
- Week 1–2: Controlled run + smoke tests; baseline metrics.
- Week 3: Stress runs + canary; full acceptance run.
- Week 4: Evaluation review, decision, and procurement handoff.

Attaching the MAP and a short outline (acceptance-tests.md) — both are stubs for review.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachment: MAP_Oxbridge_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: acceptance-tests.md (text)
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@oxbridgehealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Dan Miller <dan.miller@oxbridgehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + proposed acceptance tests for PoC

Thanks Jasmine — appreciate the clear layout. Quick notes from our side:

- Dataset: we will provide the anonymized 500-case set by Monday (clinical_500_v1.csv). Deliverable will come from our data team and include expected labels and a short data dictionary.
- Quality metric: F1 is fine, but we need Tiered thresholds — Core (>=0.90) / Preferred (>=0.92). Anything below Core fails the eval.
- Latency: Oxbridge’s minimum acceptable p50 is 150ms (we're a little more conservative on this workload given inference post-processing). Is 150ms feasible with your recommended model and 8k seq settings?
- Procurement: if eval completes successfully, procurement intends to start contract redlines the week after acceptance; we'll need a statement of expected monthly token volumes for budget.

We’re generally aligned on the timeline. One ask: please include a clear rollback trigger and a list of support contacts in the MAP. Also please add an item for security evidence: SOC2 attestation and network diagram during the handoff.

Best,
Priya Shah
Head of Clinical AI | Oxbridge Health
priya.shah@oxbridgehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-4452

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Draft MAP + proposed acceptance tests for PoC — Oxbridge asks + proposed acceptance suite

Karthik / Ben — forwarding Priya’s reply and the MAP. Key asks from Oxbridge:
- Acceptable latency p50 = 150ms (they increased from our ask).
- Tiered quality thresholds (Core >=0.90 / Preferred >=0.92).
- Security evidence (SOC2, network diagram) during procurement.
- Request for rollback triggers and support contacts.

My proposed changes to the acceptance-tests.md:
1) Smoke tests (pre-run, internal): endpoint connectivity, auth, sample inference (10 cases) — pass/fail.
2) Baseline run (500 cases): calculate precision/recall/F1 vs Oxbridge labels; performance measured p50/p95 and error counts. Must meet Core for moving forward.
3) Canary run (24h, production-like traffic): monitoring for errors and latency under 2 rps sustained; if any of these occur, we fail-forward to our smaller-quantized variant and notify Oxbridge.
4) Cutover criteria & rollback triggers:
   - Go if: Core quality met AND p50 <= 150ms AND critical errors <=2 in 72h.
   - Rollback if: sustained p95 > 800ms for >15 minutes OR >3 critical errors in 24h OR significant regression in F1 (>0.04 drop vs baseline).

Timelines I’d propose to include in the MAP (shorter cadence to match Oxbridge procurement needs):
- Tue Jul 6: dataset delivery from Oxbridge.
- Wed Jul 7–Fri Jul 9: baseline run and smoke tests.
- Mon Jul 12–Wed Jul 14: canary and stress tests.
- Thu Jul 15: joint evaluation review.

I attached a draft eval-runbook.pdf stub with run commands and the acceptance-tests.md. Thoughts?

Jasmine

Attachment: eval-runbook.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: acceptance-tests.md (text)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft MAP + proposed acceptance tests for PoC — Oxbridge asks + proposed acceptance suite

Thanks Jas — looks solid. A couple of implementation notes from the runtime/ops perspective:

- 150ms p50 is achievable on our deduped 8-bit quantized variant if we run with a warmed KV cache and continuous batching tuned to Oxbridge's traffic profile. We should call out the exact instance config in the MAP appendix (GPU type, batch target, KV cache TTL).
- Add a short post-decision contingency: if Oxbridge hits the Core threshold but not Preferred, offer a 30-day performance improvement window (config tweaks + retraining support) rather than going straight to procurement denial.
- Canary cadence: recommend a 48h canary rather than 24h to surface infrequent faults. If timelines are tight, we can compress to 24h but call that out as a risk.

I'll draft the instance config blurb and add rollback automation playbooks (pager routing + automatic fallback to quantized model) before Wed. Ben — can you add a token-volume estimate for procurement?

Karthik
VP, Technical Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@oxbridgehealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Dan Miller <dan.miller@oxbridgehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Jul 2027 14:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP + proposed acceptance tests for PoC — Final alignment

Jasmine / team — this readout is great and aligns with our internal risk appetite. Two small tweaks from procurement/security:

1) Make the canary 48h, as Karthik suggested.
2) Add the SOC2 report and the high-level network diagram to the MAP appendix (we need that for our InfoSec team).

If you can include Ben’s token-volume estimate and Karthik’s instance config/rollback automation note by end of day Wednesday (Jul 7), we’ll sign the MAP and kick off the data handoff on Thu (Jul 8). We’ll plan to issue DocuSign for the evaluation acceptance statement after the run completes.

Link to our procurement tracker: https://oxbridgehealth.atlassian.net/browse/OXB-EVAL-12

Thanks — Priya
